title: Registered lobbyists and permit consultants who presented projects at the commissions
question: Who stood up for project sponsors at the Planning and Historic Preservation hearings of 2022-2026, and did their items end differently from others of the same kind?
finding: 75 of 404 items at an address that were heard with speakers were presented by one of 20 people whose full name is in the Ethics Commission's lobbyist or permit-consultant registry; Reuben, Junius & Rose, LLP people appear on 49 of them (10 of its registrants). Their items were changed or disapproved in 31.0% of decisions against 22.7% for other items, and continued in 5.3% of cases against 9.4% expected for items of the same kinds. 3 were disapproved.
how: The SPEAKERS paragraph of every item is split into speakers. A speaker counts as a registered advocate when his or her full first and last name (common short forms such as Tom for Thomas count as the same name) matches a name in the permit-consultant registration file or the lobbyist registration file, and the speaker spoke in support or neutrally and is described, on this or another item, as presenting for the sponsor, applicant or agent. Each item (one hearing, one item number) takes its most decisive action. Only items at an address for which the minutes list at least one speaker are compared, because items on the continuance calendar usually list none. "Expected" gives each item the continuance rate of items of the same kind of approval, heard with speakers, that no registered advocate presented.
limits: A name match is labelled as such: a sponsor's architect or owner who happens to share a registrant's name would be counted; the registry's firm name is the second link, and only names that also appear presenting for a sponsor are kept. Most sponsors' representatives are not registered (an architect or the owner), so the comparison group includes represented projects too. Hiring a land-use lawyer or consultant is permitted and normal for large projects, which are also the ones most often changed by the Commission, so a difference in outcomes says more about the projects than about the advocate. Opposing advocates (for neighbors) are not counted.
